hints: Focus on what stays the same when you dilute, the moles of HCl do not change, only the volume of water around them increases.
Work out the moles you need in the end using $moles = concentration \times volume$ in $dm^3$, so $0.100 \times 0.200$.
Now test each sample the same way, converting $cm^3$ to $dm^3$ first, and look for the one that also gives that same number of moles.
walkthrough:
**Find the moles in the final solution**

Dilution adds water but no extra HCl, so moles before equals moles after. First calculate what we must end up with.

$$moles = c \times V = 0.100 \, \text{mol dm}^{-3} \times \frac{200}{1000} \, \text{dm}^{3}$$
$$moles = 0.100 \times 0.200 = 0.0200 \, \text{mol HCl}$$

**Write the rule for sample X**

For any sample, moles added is also $c \times V$. Remember to change $cm^3$ to $dm^3$ by dividing by 1000.

$$moles \, in \, X = c_X \times \frac{V_X}{1000}$$

**Test each option and match**

Let us calculate quickly:

$A: 1.00 \times 0.010 = 0.010 \, mol$

$B: 0.90 \times 0.030 = 0.027 \, mol$

$C: 0.40 \times 0.050 = 0.020 \, mol$

$D: 0.30 \times 0.100 = 0.030 \, mol$

Only one sample supplies exactly 0.0200 mol, so it will give 0.100 mol dm-3 when made up to 200 cm3.

options.A: Gives only $1.00 \times 0.010 = 0.010$ mol, which is half the 0.020 mol needed. Diluted to 200 cm3 this would give only 0.050 mol dm-3.
options.B: Gives $0.90 \times 0.030 = 0.027$ mol, which is too much. Diluted to 200 cm3 this would give 0.135 mol dm-3, higher than required.
options.C: Gives exactly $0.40 \times 0.050 = 0.020$ mol. When made up to 0.200 dm3, concentration = $0.020 / 0.200 = 0.100$ mol dm-3, a perfect match.
options.D: Gives $0.30 \times 0.100 = 0.030$ mol, which is too much. Diluted to 200 cm3 this would give 0.150 mol dm-3.
